scorecard.rationale: The dried-leaf Parkinson pilot reports cognition and salivation without an apathy result. In healthy adults, the controlled dried-leaf comparison gave higher alertness before the stress task and lower task-associated alertness after the same dose. A probable mixed-sage trial family gives no clear mood contrast. Compound studies describe movement in animals, and a Parkinson effort task uses apathy as a participant characteristic. These outcomes do not establish a directional effect on clinical apathy from dried sage. The pilot's secondary timetable and the original constituent study tables remain open.
